wiki_excerpt:
Broad Peak is the 12th highest mountain in the world at 8,051 metres (26,414 ft) elevation above sea level. It is one of the eight-thousanders, and is located in the Karakoram range spanning Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan, and Xinjiang, China. The first ascent of this mountain was in June 1957, accomplished by Fritz Wintersteller, Marcus Schmuck, Kurt Diemberger, and Hermann Buhl as part of an Austrian expedition.


Geography
Broad Peak is part of the Gasherbrum massif in Baltistan situated on the border of Pakistan and China. It is located in the Karakoram mountain range, approximately eight kilometres (five miles) from K2. The peak's name aptly describes its physical characteristics, with a summit that extends over 1.5 kilometres (7⁄8 mile) in length, giving it the appearance of a "broad peak."
In addition to the main summit (8051 m), two of the mountain's subsidiary peaks are eight-thousanders: Rocky Summit (8028 m) and Broad Peak Central (8011 m), with Broad Peak North (7490 m), and Kharut Kangri (6942 m) being the other two peaks.


Etymology
The literal translation of "Broad Peak" to Falchan Kangri is not used among the Balti people. The English name was introduced in 1892 by the British explorer Martin Conway, in reference to the similarly named Breithorn in the Alps.


Climbing history
The first known ascent of Broad Peak was achieved between 8 and 9 June 1957, by Fritz Wintersteller, Marcus Schmuck, Kurt Diemberger, and Hermann Buhl of an Austrian expedition led by Marcus Schmuck. A first attempt by the team was made on 29 May where Fritz Wintersteller and Kurt Diemberger reached the forepeak (8,030 m). The first ascent took the West Spur and was accomplished without the aid of supplemental oxygen, high-altitude porters, or base camp support.
In July 2007, an Austrian mountaineering team climbed Broad Peak and retrieved the corpse of Markus Kronthaler, who had died on the mountain one year before, from over 8,000 metres.
In 2008, French mountaineer Élisabeth Revol made solo ascents of Broad Peak, Gasherbrum I and Gasherbrum II within 16 days and without the aid of supplemental oxygen.
In the winter and summer of 2009, there were no summits. There was one winter expedition by a Polish-Canadian team. In the summer there was one fatality, Cristina Castagna.
In the summer of 2012, five members of "Koroška 8000", a Slovenian team led by Gregor Lačen, summitted the mountain without supplementary oxygen or high-altitude porters. They established a route in deep snow from Camp 4 to the summit, used by seven additional climbers from other expeditions. All summitted on 31 July 2012.
On 5 March 2013, Maciej Berbeka, Adam Bielecki, Tomasz Kowalski and Artur Małek made the first winter ascent and conquered the mountain peak without oxygen during the winter. Broad Peak was the twelfth eight-thousander summited in wintertime and the tenth eight-thousander first summitted in winter by the Polish climbers.

grok_lead: Broad Peak, also known as Falchan Kangri, is a prominent eight-thousander in the Karakoram mountain range, straddling the border between Gilgit-Baltistan in Pakistan and Xinjiang in China. It stands at an elevation of 8,051 meters (26,414 feet), making it the twelfth-highest mountain in the world and one of the four 8,000-meter peaks in the Karakoram. The mountain's name derives from its exceptionally broad summit ridge, which spans about 1.5 kilometers and features multiple summits, including the main peak, a central summit (Broad Peak Central) at 8,011 meters, a rocky summit at 8,028 meters, and a north summit at 7,490 meters. First sighted in 1856 by British surveyor T.G. Montgomerie, who designated it K3, the peak was later renamed "Broad Peak" during a 1892 expedition led by William Martin Conway due to its wide, flat-topped appearance. The first successful ascent occurred on June 9, 1957, achieved without supplemental oxygen by an Austrian expedition comprising Hermann Buhl, Fritz Wintersteller, Kurt Diemberger, and Marcus Schmuck, who followed the standard west ridge route from the base camp on the Godwin-Austen Glacier. This alpine-style climb, completed in just 22 days from base camp, marked the sixth eight-thousander first summited, after Annapurna, Everest, K2, Cho Oyu, and Lhotse, highlighting the peak's relative accessibility among high-altitude giants despite its formidable height. Broad Peak is renowned in mountaineering circles for its moderate technical difficulty compared to steeper neighbors like K2, yet it poses significant challenges including avalanche-prone slopes, a crux rock step on the upper ridge, and notorious false summits that have led to navigational errors. The standard west ridge route remains the most popular, involving a 3,150-meter elevation gain from base camp at approximately 4,900 meters, often requiring fixed ropes and multiple acclimatization rotations. As of 2024, more than 400 ascents have been documented, with a fatality rate of approximately 8%, underscoring the inherent risks of high-altitude climbing on this massif.
